Chloe — taking this. Draft below (will attach a refined PDF + workbook later).

Wave-based Activation (high level):
- Wave 0 (preflight, 1 week): shadow traffic at 100% of sample rate; smoke tests, telemetry baselines, and live KV cache warm-ups. Exit criteria: 24h with no errors >1% API error rate, end-to-end P50 latency within target band, and full instrumentation in place.
- Wave 1 (pilot customers, 2 days): 2% production traffic to the new serving cluster via weighted routing. Success metric: <2% user-facing errors and automated SLO checks pass for 48 hours. Canary will be promoted if metrics stable and manual review signed off.
- Wave 2 (regional expansion, 7 days): increase to 20% traffic, enable regional caching lanes, monitor cost-per-token and tail latency.
- Wave 3 (ramp to steady state, 3-7 days): 100% routed to new environment with rollback guardrails in place.

Rollback / Short-circuit rules (automated):
- Instant rollback: fatal health-checks (model server down), TLS certificate issues, or depletion of reserved GPU capacity.
- Threshold rollback: sustained 5-minute window where P99 latency exceeds 2x baseline OR error rate exceeds threshold configured per route (default 3%).
- Manual rollback: operator-initiated via console; recommended when degradation is isolated to a subset of tenants.

I will add a simple decision tree graphic to the seq_playbook.xlsx and include the traffic weights used for each step.

Ben
Director, Solutions Engineering

Hi Amir — quick summary on keys/logs:

KMS and key separation:
- Customers may bring-your-own KMS: Redwood supports static key wrapping via customer-managed keys in AWS KMS, Google KMS, or Azure Key Vault. We also provide an HSM-backed option for at-rest model checkpoint encryption.
- During migration we use transient key-wrapping for in-flight exports; no plaintext model artifacts are written to shared buckets. Each tenancy is assigned a separate key alias to enforce separation.

Audit logs and tenancy separation:
- Audit logs are written to a tenant-scoped S3/GCS path (or forwarded to customer SIEM) with immutable retention controls; access is role-gated.
- During wave mirrors, logs are tagged with wave-id and traffic-tag to make reconciliation trivial. Retention windows are configurable (default 90 days).

I attached a short appendix (ACME_RFI_Implementation_Answers_v1.pdf) with the control-plane APIs we expect you to call during activation (list-keys, rotate-key, export-logs) and the recommended IAM roles.

LMK if you need a short diagram for the mirrored logging flow — I included a baseline diagram (wave-mirror-diagram.png) in the attachments.

Best,
Laura
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

1) For Wave 1 (pilot), can you confirm whether traffic weighting happens at our edge (we use AWS ALB + Lambda) or within Redwood's routing tier? We prefer routing decisions be observable in our infra.
2) For the automated threshold rollback, is there a cooldown period where you prevent flip-flopping?

Also, can you provide an example runbook row showing who is on-call and the exact console commands/API calls to promote or rollback a canary? That would help our ops team sign off.

Amir — attaching the consolidated packet and a sample runbook row. Quick answers inline: 

1) Routing observability: We support both approaches. For customers who prefer edge-based weighting (ALB/LB), Redwood will export a signed routing-map JSON and we will tag requests with x-redwood-wave-id so your telemetry can attribute traffic. If you prefer Redwood-managed routing, we will provide a pre-authenticated read-only view into the routing decision stream for the pilot.

2) Cooldown: yes — automated threshold rollbacks have a default cooldown of 10 minutes to avoid flip-flop, configurable per-project. The seq_playbook.xlsx contains the exact parameter keys (cooldown_ms, evaluation_window_ms, threshold_pct).

Attached: ACME_RFI_Implementation_Answers_v1.pdf, seq_playbook.xlsx, wave-mirror-diagram.png

Next step: can we book a 45-minute run-through with your ops on Thursday 17:00 PT? I can have Ben demo the promotion/rollback sequence and Markus walk through resource guardrails.

Thanks,
Chloe
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
